deities: Shiva (Parshuram Mahadev - rock-carved cave sanctum); natural rock figures of Ganesha and Shiva
festivals: Fairs on Shravan Shukla Shashti and Saptami (August-September; two fairs annually)

history.dynasty: None (mythological rock-cut cave; one source calls it ~1000 years old - weakly sourced)
history.period: Unknown antiquity (legendary; ~1000 years old per one travel source - verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: Parshuram Mahadev is NOT in Pali city - it is a cave temple on the Pali-Rajsamand district border, about 14 km from Sadri town and ~10 km from Kumbhalgarh Fort. Wikipedia reports the main cave temple falls in Rajsamand district while Kund Dham comes in Desuri tehsil of Pali district - district attribution is genuinely contested; verify. Legend says Parshuram, the sixth avatar of Vishnu, cut the cave from the Aravalli rock with his axe and performed penance here before a self-manifested Shivlinga. The whole cave is in one rock, ~3,995 ft above sea level, with naturally formed Ganesh-Shiva figures and nine kunds that never dry. Reached by 500 steps down from the Sadri-side parking; it is called the 'Amarnath of Rajasthan'. Over 900,000 visitors annually per one source (verify). Coordinates are street-level near Sadri, ~14 km from the cave - approximate.

name: Parshuram Mahadev Temple
town: Sadri, Desuri tehsil, Pali district (CSV town 'Pali' is imprecise - the temple is ~14 km from Sadri on the Pali-Rajsamand border)
town_description: Sadri is a town at the Aravalli foothills in Desuri tehsil of Pali district, on the Falna-Kumbhalgarh corridor. It is a small pilgrimage base known for its own Jain temples and as the easiest access point (500 steps) to the Parshuram Mahadev cave shrine in the hills above.

travel.airport: Udaipur Airport - about 100 km (verify); Jodhpur Airport - about 160 km (verify).
travel.railway: Falna and Rani railway stations are the nearest (verify distances).
travel.road: About 14 km from Sadri town; then 500 steps down to the cave. Also reachable by a winding trekking route from the Kumbhalgarh side parking.

visitor_information.best_time: August-September for the Shravan fairs; otherwise October to March (the cave area is lush in monsoon).
